findings.message: The test skips the guard-line check for any script whose text contains `from clutch.__main__ import main`. After the alias fix, `tests/regress_requisition_prior_review.py` and `tests/regress_review_intakes_own_stem.py` contain `from clutch.__main__ import main as clutch_main`, which matches that substring. So the test never checks that these two files contain `if __name__ == "__main__":`. Acceptance criterion 3 says each of the ten files must contain that line, checked by this test. The skip also lets any future script that imports `clutch.__main__` avoid the text check.
findings.paved_road: Remove the `if "from clutch.__main__ import main" not in ...` condition and assert `'if __name__ == "__main__":' in script.read_text()` for every globbed script. All 54 scripts now have the guard, including those that import `clutch_main`.
